tasks.title: Cell registry 1/5: registry module, management CLI, single grid module
tasks.notes: Part of the cell-registry epic (tickets 29-33, one new branch off main, one PR; do NOT use the bakeoff-r004 branch). DESIGN (agreed in grilling session): world data lives in the active world: registry/cells.json + registry/features.json, sparse (absent cell = empty), written ONLY through one registry module (atomic write, sorted keys); LLM reads only via a documented management command. Cell record: ground none|ghost|ghost+features|generated; trees bool; decor bool; marker up|none; hold reason|null. Derived, never stored: empty, DONE, current cell (= marker cell), a cell's features. DONE = ground generated + trees + decor + every registered feature in the cell built + no marker + no open OSM-coverage warnings. Feature record: id = build slug (matches site/builds/<name>.json), name, cells touched, status planned|in-progress|built (one status per feature). Invariants enforced in code (refused write raises error naming the rule, nothing changes): single marker; ghost+features only on ghost ground; trees/decor only on generated ground; rebuilding ground clears trees+decor; reopening a feature clears trees+decor in every cell it touches. Management CLI with clear docs: query (is feature X built, what is left in cell C, status), register feature (explicit list; helper proposes OSM candidates), hold set/clear, dismiss OSM warning with reason. GRID: one cellmath module owns cell size, bounds, cell->region mapping, ring order, parse_cell and the id format; delete the other definitions (world_frame.CELL/cell_of/cell_bounds/parse_cell, coverage.cell_of/cell_bbox, pass_mask.CELL_SIZE, site_stages.CELL_SHIFT, ground_sources.mc_tile_for_cell, ref_manifest.mc_tile_id, lidar_ghost use of CELL_SHIFT). Cell id is always the string 'tx,tz' (e.g. 48,-44); 'm44' spelling only inside file names. Origin cell and cell size move into the world's world-frame.json (remove hard-coded ORIGIN_CELL in cellmath.py and CENTRE in site_status.py). Tests for all invariants. Done 2026-10-21 on cell-registry-tickets: scripts/cell_registry.py + CLI; cellmath owns grid (size/origin from world-frame cell); invariant tests; callers delegate. World checkout: config/world-frame.json cell block + empty registry/.

tasks.title: Cell registry 2/5: make build commands update the registry automatically
tasks.notes: PRINCIPLE: the registry is updated by code as a side effect of build commands, not by LLM-followed rules. ground_layer/trees_layer/decor_layer set ground/trees/decor on a clean readback only. site_kit.apply: feature status in-progress on begin, built only on clean readback (zero mismatches; mismatches stay in-progress); cells touched overwritten from the real footprint. cell_marker raise/clear sets marker (marker no longer counts as work or as a STAGES entry). lidar_ghost keeps its state machine but writes only to the registry: ghost lay-down around the marker cell (default ring 2; ground none->ghost / ghost+features); real feature apply strips ghost features first (ghost+features -> ghost); real ground apply -> generated and drops ghost features; markers never count as real work. Every block-removing command clears the matching flags in the same step: mask_undo, strip_cell_above_ground, ghost supersede/strip, site_recover. A failed apply never sets flags. Feature specs stay in site/builds/<name>.json; *-cells.json ownership files stay as block-level evidence the registry points to (not a second status record). Per-run detail (readback, snapshot, structure/from/to) goes to the existing *-result.json / *-backup.json; masks stay under verification/site/masks. Tests per writer. Done 2026-10-21 on cell-registry-tickets: registry_hooks + site_kit.apply begin/clean, cell_marker raise/clear/adopt, mask_undo, strip_cell_above_ground, site_recover rollback, lidar_ghost feature strip demotion. Tests: test_registry_hooks + site_recover apply cases.

tasks.title: Cell registry 3/5: replace STAGES, QUEUE, handoff, sign-offs, holds, AERIAL-REVIEW, CURRENT-CELL; add next + issues; rewrite orchestrator
tasks.notes: DELETE: per-cell STAGES.json (all readers - cell_gaps, layers_done, requeue_plan, real_work_started, ground_done, site_status, site_pages, site_recover, lump_scan - read the registry instead); QUEUE.txt + Q-nnn ids + site_handoff queue writing/advance_to_next_cell + .handoff-pending.json + set_pending/clear_pending + the whole handoff system; COVERAGE-SIGNOFFS.jsonl and ALL sign-off code, rules, docs, tests (system runs unsupervised); CELL-HOLDS.jsonl (becomes cell hold field); AERIAL-REVIEW.txt and its code (site_handoff.py ~147-247); CURRENT-CELL.json and every other way of tracking the current cell (coverage.focus_cell, site_status centre, queue 'marker must be up' text); coverage.cell_rollup (COVERAGE.txt generated block now produced from the registry). KEEP/ADD: `next` registry command, read-only and deterministic (idempotent): open issues first, then next undone item. Cell choice: marker cell if not DONE, else nearest undone non-held cell to the configured origin ordered by distance then clockwise ring order from north (the build task raises the marker, next does not). Order inside a cell: ground, then features in registry order, then trees, then decor. ISSUES.txt = snagging backlog, one parsed line per issue with a registry target and reason, e.g. 'I-014  cell 48,-44 trees  <why>' / 'I-015  feature q001_university_road_42  <why>'; target is cell layer, feature id or whole cell; add-issue command reopens the target; auto-closes on clean rebuild and archives with date. Rewrite cell-orchestrator skill as a thin loop: run next, launch one subagent per task (a cell layer, a feature, or an issue), wait; a handoff is just a fresh session running next. Update human-confirm-fix and redo skills accordingly. DONE: registry next + ISSUES/add-issue/auto-close; cell_gaps/layers_done/ground_done/focus/lidar real_work/site_status marker from registry; QUEUE advance/cmd_next redirected; aerial-review + coverage signoffs retired as progress; orchestrator/redo/confirm-fix rewritten. tasks.title: Cell registry 4/5: repair cell, whole-world backup pair, logout gate, verify
tasks.notes: repair <cell>: back up ONLY the impacted region files (region holding the cell plus any region its features/trees/decor spill into, from *-cells.json footprints and masks) together with that cell's registry record; wipe only that cell's columns to air above bedrock; replay from the registry clipped to the cell bounds (ghost ground/features if ghost state, else ground, features in registry order, trees, decor; features from site/builds specs); re-raise marker if it was up; if any step fails, clear flags for that step and all later ones so next picks it up. 'undo repair' restores the region files and the saved registry record. Bake-off: wipe the WHOLE world each round, restore ONE whole-world backup paired with a whole-registry copy (no per-cell slices); update model_bakeoff.restore_ghost_step and region_backup. Raw region_backup restore of a partial snapshot is refused (error points at the proper undo/redo command) except via repair-undo and the full-world bake-off restore. LOGOUT GATE: every command that rewrites region files (repair, undo repair, bake-off wipe/restore, dryrun_reset) refuses without --confirm-logged-out, stops and plays the need-you sound asking the user to log out; second guard checks session.lock / a running server holding the save and refuses even with the flag. VERIFY (report only, exit non-zero on any error): invariants; marker rings vs registry (exactly the marked cell has a stripe ring); region files exist for cells with ground and no blocks in cells the registry calls empty; built features have ownership files and blocks still present; registered features have specs; OSM buildings no registered feature covers (warnings that block DONE until resolved or dismissed with a reason); leftover old-system files (STAGES, QUEUE, CURRENT-CELL, sign-offs). Hook verify into scripts/run_tests.py / dryrun_reset where sensible. DONE: logout_gate (--confirm-logged-out + session.lock/MCP refuse); region_backup kind partial/whole-world/repair + snap-world; raw restore refuses partial; registry_repair backup/undo/replay-plan/clear-flags; cell_registry repair|undo-repair|verify; model_bakeoff restore-ghost; dryrun_reset logout gate + post-reset verify. Partial: live feature/trees/decor replay still raises to manual CLI; full OSM/block verify and bake-off per-round wipe deferred toward #33.

tasks.title: ship-branch skill: build, review, fix, merge loop
tasks.notes: Project skill under .claude/skills/. Builder session finishing a code change runs: tests, then a fresh-context read-only reviewer subagent on Sonnet at high effort, then a normal-tier fixer (default model, normal effort, same worktree) on blockers, re-review, up to 3 review rounds, then ship_branch.py merge. Tests failing before review go to the fixer and count toward the cap. If main moved, the fixer merges main into the branch; re-review only if the resolution touched more than conflict markers. Reviewer brief is fixed: branch diff vs main, CODING_STANDARDS.md, GLOSSARY.md, accepted ADRs, ticket text, test coverage; returns APPROVE or CHANGES with blocker/nit findings; never edits. Only blockers loop; nits become tracker follow-ups or are dropped if trivial. Ask the owner before using Opus or any other high-cost model; everything else is automatic. Opt-outs in the owner's words: 'no review'/'skip review' (build, test, merge) and 'leave on branch'/'don't merge' (stop after build, report branch; implies no review). A ticket may carry review: skip. Cap hit or any stop: leave the branch unmerged and play need-you. Check by running it on one trivial real change. Bootstrapping: #61-#63 themselves are built on task/* branches and merged by the orchestrator after a manual pass. Merged via wave 61-65: .claude/skills/ship-branch/SKILL.md on main.

tasks.title: Add bidirectional XYZ tile positions, pixel offsets and batch conversion
tasks.notes: Approved plan 2026-10-25; depends on #84. Extend scripts/world_frame.py as the canonical coordinate interface, reusing existing XYZ/Web Mercator maths rather than adding a competing tool. Forward: accept zoom plus either latitude/longitude or Minecraft x,z; return tile code zoom/x/y plus east_px and south_px. Reverse: accept tile code and pixel offsets; return latitude/longitude or Minecraft x,z using an explicit frame or the explicitly selected active world. Agreed offset convention: floating-point pixels from the northwest corner of a 256-pixel logical tile; east increases rightward, south increases downward; offsets are not northings and do not depend on downloaded image resolution. Preserve fractional precision and existing Minecraft rounding behaviour. Extend to-wm and add from-wm with structured JSON output; provide JSON batch input from a file or stdin, reuse the single-point conversion functions and preserve input order. Latitude/longitude-only conversion must work with no selected world; Minecraft conversion requires explicit or explicitly selected world-frame configuration. Support integer zooms 0 through 30, canonical longitude [-180,180), valid Web Mercator latitudes and finite coordinates; reject malformed/out-of-range tile indices and offsets outside [0,256). Permanent tests cover known tile positions, fractional offsets, tile edges, both hemispheres, forward/reverse conversions, fictional Minecraft frames, batches, empty batches and invalid inputs; use fixed expected values and no GDAL, network or real-world checkout data. Audit existing helpers, CLIs and AI instructions for overlapping coordinate-conversion routes, including world_frame, ref_manifest, geo and provider adapters. Consolidate conversion maths into world_frame; retain necessary compatibility wrappers only as delegates. Update AI-facing documentation, skills and CLI help to teach one preferred single-point and batch interface, including offset units/directions, coordinate ordering, world selection and runnable examples. Keep tile-image fetching and evidence-sheet generation documented as distinct capabilities. Done when: both directions and batch mode work through one canonical implementation; permanent tests cover the agreed cases independently of current world; AI guidance contains no competing conversion implementations or contradictory instructions. GDAL remains allowed for appropriate bulk-file geospatial processing. | Merged 2026-10-25 ship_branch (75d55e1 + 5b0676b / merge e066671). Bidirectional XYZ + batch; reject exact ±WM_MAX_LAT. Scope: STRICTLY READ-ONLY reader of .mca files (never write, copy, snap, restore or delete region files), implemented as an adapter behind BlockStore (read/read_many) so planners are unchanged; used for planning and dry-run reads after a server save (server_save_all_worlds; rules/process.md already says save before reading region files). Open questions to answer first: does anything in planning need live state not on disk (unsaved chunks, entities, block entities); how to detect stale reads (save then read; compare chunk timestamps); chunk formats/version (DataVersion 4903); reuse an existing NBT/anvil library vs write minimal; keep dependency count low. tasks.title: Bug: real ground drops ghost-ground ownership across the whole cell, so undo restores air instead of the substrate (cause of #123 pit)
tasks.notes: ROOT CAUSE of #123 (found 2026-10-26 from journal + blobs only, read-only, world southampton-build). Undo restore values come from cell_journal._prepare_undo (lib/journal/cell_journal.py ~1168): erase[p] = under-owner state (ownership with the target seqs skipped) else AIR. Ownership comes from _cell_owners (~812), which at line ~831 deletes EVERY ghost-ground owner in a cell as soon as a real 'ground' build lands there ('real ground supersedes ghost ground'). That assumes the real ground apply physically overwrote all ghost blocks, but a ground plan writes only its own positions (highfield_48_m44_ground seq 104/110: n=7586 for the whole cell, surface only, nothing under features). The ghost substrate below (stone y1-52, top concrete y53) is still in the world but no journal entry owns it, so undo falls back to air. JUBILEE NUMBERS: undo seq 114 (n=36756): in cell 48,-44, 10003 positions written as air where ghost_48_m44_ground (seq 68) has solid blocks. These are the pit: e.g. 6244,-5515 build 90 wrote stone y49-52 + smooth_stone y53 over ghost stone/black_concrete; undo wrote air y49-53, exactly the 5-block pit with vertical walls (the edge is the jubilee footprint). In cells 48,-43 / 49,-44 / 49,-43 (no real ground yet) undo correctly restored the ghost blocks (10878+713+1934 positions). Contract pinned by lib/journal/test_cell_journal.py:384 test_ghost_ground_then_real_ground_supersedes (line 392 asserts that a ghost block the ground plan never wrote is unowned), ADR 004 point 5 and docs/specs/cell-journal-interface.md:68. SECONDARY GAP (same fix area): with no owner anywhere, undo assumes air, so blocks in the world that no journal entry owns are lost. At x=6209 z -5513..-5505 before_jubilee has stone to y53 while ghost 68/12 top is y49 (light_gray/black concrete); undo will leave a 4-block step there even with the supersession fixed. Where those blocks came from is unknown (not any journalled plan in these cells). FIX: (1) supersession only where the real ground covers: per column the ground plan writes, drop ghost owners above that column's real top (and at its positions, already handled by later-wins); keep the ghost substrate below and every ghost column the ground plan does not cover (under features). Update test 384 and add a test: ghost ground, feature over it, real ground elsewhere in the cell, undo feature -> ghost blocks restored, no air. Check what reconcile and the ghost.ground view now report for the kept substrate (it must not be 'missing' or re-queue ghost ground). (2) journal the prior blocks at Build begin (read_many over the planned positions, stored as a second blob, e.g. 'prior'); undo uses the under-owner when it is a real owner, else the prior blob, else air (old entries without a prior blob keep today's rule). Benchmark the read on a ~60k-block feature. (3) ADR 004 / interface spec: record the narrower supersession and the prior-blob rule. DONE WHEN: a scratch-world build + real ground in the same cell + undo leaves the box identical to before_<plan> (structure diff, zero differences), with tests for both rules. If it works, #123 closes with it (its remaining steps are the readback-vs-snapshot check, the purge-skill step and the jubilee repair). Landed on main via ship_branch (task/124-ghost-ground-ownership, bfd95d8).

tasks.title: Bug: element undo digs into intact ground (pit after purging a feature); undo must restore the actual pre-build world
tasks.notes: FOUND purging jubilee_w93729745 (2026-10-26, world southampton-build, cells 48,-44 / 48,-43 / 49,-44 / 49,-43). Journal: build begin seq 90 (strict False, modifies [], blob 71b85862caf886865f515ea3110daf21, n=61627), undo begin seq 114 (strict True, targets [90], blob 7a1bf5423a5cc3fe4434c72a19b0f405, n=36756). Structures: southampton_refine:before_jubilee_w93729745 and before_undo_jubilee_w93729745_20261026225610, both box (6208,37,-5535)-(6279,67,-5472). SYMPTOM: a pit about 5 blocks deep, vertical walls, around x 6244 z -5508..-5525. Live top_y (first free block) there is 49, before-snapshot 54. z -5500 and -5530 match. 17 sampled columns, not a full diff. EVIDENCE (read-only): (a) the build did NOT dig: in before_jubilee and before_undo the ground below y=53 is identical (stone y44-52 at 6244,-5520 and 6244,-5515; only y53 differs, black_concrete vs smooth_stone floor). Only 43 positions were solid before but air at undo time. (b) The undo's blob writes different ground than the real pre-build world: for x=6209, z -5513..-5505 it writes air over y37-53 where before_jubilee has stone to 53; at z -5504 it writes stone to y48 then concrete at 49. So undo restored a stale ground model (surface about y49) instead of the world as it was before the build (surface about y53/54). Likely cause: the restore values come from the journal's ground-owner plan (ghost_48_m43_ground etc.), which disagrees with the real before state. Not confirmed; read lib/site/site_kit.py undo (line ~1064) and cell_journal first. WHY IT WAS MISSED: undo's clean readback passed (it checks against its own targets) and cell_registry reconcile showed only 62 ground findings (40 missing, 22 foreign), which --fix repaired. Neither compares with the before_<plan> structure. HOW TO COMPARE: structure_file_read returns base64 gzip NBT (too big for chat, it lands in a tool-results file); parse with lib/blocks/nbt_read.py read_named_root (lists are Tag.value=(kind, items); pos is relative to the box origin). block_get_top_y returns the first free y, so the top solid block is one lower. RegionBlocks (lib/blocks/region_blocks.py) reads the world read-only after a save. Blob format: zstd json {rle: [[x,z,y0,y1,state]]}. PLAN: (1) reproduce on a small feature in a scratch world: build, undo, diff the box against before_<plan>; (2) find where undo takes its restore values and make them the begin-time snapshot of the actual world, or journal the prior blocks at apply; (3) make undo readback compare the whole box with the before_<plan> structure and fail on any difference; (4) regression test in lib/site/test_element_undo.py; (5) purge skill step 3: compare the footprint with the snapshot, not only reconcile. JUBILEE REPAIR (separate, world work): restore_structure_backup.py jubilee_w93729745 dry run, then cell_registry reconcile; it bypasses the journal. CAUSE FOUND (2026-10-26): see #124. Not the ground-owner plan disagreeing with the world in general: in cell 48,-44 the real highfield ground (seq 104/110) made the fold drop all ghost-ground ownership in that cell, so undo had no earlier owner under jubilee and wrote air (10003 positions; the pit). A smaller unowned-block gap (x=6209 strip) is also covered by #124. #124 is the prerequisite; if its scratch-world undo diff is clean, close #123 alongside it after the jubilee repair and the purge-skill check. UNBLOCKED after #124: ownership + prior-blob fix landed. Remaining for #123: undo readback-vs-before_<plan> structure check; purge skill footprint-vs-snapshot step; jubilee world repair (restore_structure_backup + reconcile) — world work. DONE 2026-10-26: undo begin compares erase plan to before_<plan> structure and abandons on drift (verify_erase_matches_before); structure_nbt reader; element_undo regression tests; purge §3 footprint-vs-snapshot. Jubilee pit repaired live (1712 stone fills where substrate was air; structure_load failed on size — fill path). Merge via ship_branch.

tasks.title: Pitched roofs over lidar ridges in zoned features
tasks.notes: Cause: feature_build requires roofs[label].kind == flat for any label with a zones entry (feature_build.py:503); assign_roof_zones snaps the DSM to plateau levels, so a ridge becomes stepped flat terraces. roof_pitched (single hip from the footprint edge) cannot express wings at different heights, so zoned buildings cannot be pitched at all. The West Building designer also read 'flat roof behind brick parapet' from a street photo without checking the lidar profile. Evidence: lidar DSM over West (w34391673) rises and falls across its wings, 48->52->48 and 49->56->51 m AOD; the spec snapped it to 44/48/51/54. Covers issue I-009 (roof built flat where the real building has a pitched roof), snag S-013. Scope: allow kind pitched with zones; within each zone, where the DSM shows a ridge, build stair-slab slopes from the zone eave up to the ridge along the ridge line; plateaus stay flat. One line in the design brief: check the lidar profile before calling a roof flat. Done when a dry run of west_w34391673 shows a ridge along the lidar ridge line and SUSU's flat roof is unchanged. Check line S-013: West's roof rises to a ridge where the lidar shows one, with no stepped flat terraces. One regression test only; no new gates or lints. | Merged task/125-pitched-roofs-zones @ bfc4157 via ship_branch.

tasks.title: Features stay in the cell plan: undo clears the build only
tasks.notes: Cause: a feature enters a cell's view only through its first apply ('A feature is registered by its first apply; there is no register command', cell_registry.py), and CellRegistry.view skips undone builds (cell_journal.py ~996), so an undone feature vanishes from the cell: after Jubilee was undone (2026-10-26 22:56) status for 48,-44 lists only Retail, SUSU and West, and 'left' is just decor and the marker. propose-features (cell_features.missing_features) finds the University Road houses but nothing records them. Covers issue I-012 (houses and undone features drop out of the cell's obligations), snag S-011. Scope: a cell plan in the journal: a note kind recording each feature or house a cell must have, written from propose-features (an option to record its candidates). The view lists planned-but-unbuilt features under 'left'; 'done' needs each one built. Undo clears the build only: the feature stays in the plan as not built, so next offers it for a redo. Dismissing is a separate, deliberate act with a reason (e.g. 'car park, not a building'); undo never dismisses. Owner calls: the note kind's name; whether next offers features before ground (left open by #118). Done when, in a journal fixture, undoing a built feature keeps it under 'left' and next offers it, and a recorded house stays under 'left' until built or dismissed with a reason. Check line S-011: the University Road houses and Jubilee show under 'left' for 48,-44 until they are built. One regression test only; no new gates or lints. | Merged task/128-cell-plan-undo @ 9925c19 via ship_branch.

tasks.title: Ground takes bare-terrain lidar height, not the surface top
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the decor-blocks-in-the-roadway issue (I-026, snags S-034 and S-031); independent review applied. Cause class: Translation. Owner's layering rule: there are two lidar products, surface (DSM) and bare terrain (DTM); the difference is objects (cars, planters, kiosks, features). Ground uses the terrain; decor and features build the objects; trees use the difference only to help place trees. Today ground_heights (lib/layers/ground_layer.py about lines 488-511) takes the heightmap 'base' for every column, and base is the surface top: in providers/ukdefra-lidar/manage/defra_world.py heightmap() (about lines 64-95) ground is the DTM height, feature is DSM minus DTM, top is ground plus feature and base = where(tree, ground, top), so only tree columns get the terrain height. The DTM is computed there (ground_y) but not exported, so Maps.get(x, z, 'base') cannot reach it. Cars, kiosks and planters were therefore raised into roads and paving, with dirt beneath. Deliver: (1) the heightmap dict gains a 'terrain' array (the DTM ground height heightmap() already computes); (2) Maps.get accepts the field 'terrain'; (3) lidar_base_map and ground_heights use it for free columns; footprint and roof columns keep 'base'; (4) where a provider or a live Maps has no 'terrain', ground falls back to 'base'; (5) fix the lidar_heightmap.py docstring that calls base 'top of solid ground' and the wording in rules/evidence-order.md. Scope: this fixes road and paving bumps only; the 'blocks instead of hedges' part is a decor matter. Cost to note: once ground stops raising objects, decor and features must place them, or cars and planters vanish; check the decor tasks before relying on that. Files: providers/ukdefra-lidar/manage/defra_world.py, lib/sources/lidar_heightmap.py, lib/layers/ground_layer.py, lib/sources/test_defra_world.py, lib/layers/test_ground_layer.py, rules/evidence-order.md. Proof: a unit test where a column's surface sits above its terrain and ground does not raise it. Check: name the command in the task for a before and after count of road and paving columns above their neighbours' median on a rerun (expect near 0), plus an in-game look at the road in the snag. Related: #167 (ground height from lidar, done). Helps: every ground pass in every world on a lidar baseline.

tasks.notes:
Raised 2026-10-28 from the SUSU entrance covered-area issue (I-021, snag S-027; also the covered-entrance part of I-018). Cause class: Capability. facade_plan entrances accept and validate awning_like (lib/builds/facade_plan.py) but plan_doors in lib/builds/feature_build.py never reads it; awning_like is only built from free-standing details rows. Not verified: what the SUSU portal photos show at each entrance. Deliver: after the shell and roof are built (as details() does, so the roof pass does not overwrite it), a cover is placed over each placed entrance whose awning_like.kind is not none. Two geometries: awning and covered_area = a row of roof-material bottom-half slabs at door top + 1, as wide as the door leaves plus 1 block each side, extending out `depth` blocks over the step-out (depth default 1 when absent or 0; covered_area simply uses the larger depth, no wall carving); porch_roof = the same slab roof plus a post at each outer front corner standing on the step-out ground. Cells inside the building mass are skipped; the door stays walkable. Unresolved entrances and kind none build nothing. Dry-run prints `door <id> cover <kind> depth <n>`. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, colocated tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py (one per kind, none builds nothing, depth changes extent, unresolved entrance builds no cover, existing details awning_like row unchanged), rules/feature-builds.md (geometry per kind, plan_doors reads it). The spec edit that adds awning_like to the SUSU entrance (susu_w33830305) is part of the check, not the code change: the designer or rebuild adds it after reading the photo. Check S-027: after rebuilding susu_w33830305 with an awning_like entry on its entrance, a roof stands over the door in game and the door is still walkable.

tasks.title: logout_gate: work without fcntl (Windows)
tasks.notes:

Replace with a portable check (msvcrt.locking on Windows, or try opening the lock file exclusively). Keep the rule that session.lock existence proves nothing. Add a test with a fake lock.

tasks.title: lidar_extremes: suggested y_offset can push tops over 319
tasks.notes:
providers/ukdefra-lidar/review/lidar_extremes.py reports suggested_y_offset_for_ground_near_64, which only aims the DTM minimum near 64. For Ventnor (DTM 0-243 m, DSM 275 m) it suggested an offset that would put tops at 339, above the 319 build limit; the agent had to override it. Make the suggestion respect both limits (ground min >= -64 with margin, DSM max <= 319), or say plainly when no offset fits.

tasks.notes:

tasks.title: Tile-aligned bbox pulls in extra lidar tiles (new-world-build skill and tiles_for)
tasks.notes: 2026-10-28, Sheffield bootstrap: bbox-mc 430000,-390000,440000,-385000 (exactly tile-aligned, 2 tiles intended) fetched 6 tiles / 12 downloads (about 900 MB, not 300 MB). Cause: defra_lidar.tiles_for adds 1 m east and north for bilinear corners, so a box ending exactly on a tile edge reaches the next tile column and row. Not a bug in tiles_for, but the new-world-build skill promises 1 tile (aligned) / 2 / 4 and never says to end an aligned box 1 m inside the upper edge (e.g. x1=439998). Fix: say so in the skill section 0 and the tile-count step, or have lidar_extremes warn when the box ends on a tile edge and print the tile count before fetching. Done: new-world-build skill now says to end an aligned box 1 m inside the upper edge (docs-only, no tool change).

tasks.title: Zoned flat roofs write the full-block name for slab-family materials, and the dry run warns on unknown block ids
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the flat-roof-writes-a-nonexistent-block issue (I-027, snags S-035, S-039); independent review applied. Cause class: Translation. In lib/builds/feature_build.py the zoned build writes the roof deck as self.set(x, ry, z, rm) (about line 1740) with the raw material name; only pitched_roof_states maps names through block_family_variants (_ROOF_FULL_NAME, deepslate_tile to deepslate_tiles). So a zoned flat roof asking for deepslate_tile wrote minecraft:deepslate_tile, which does not exist, and the roof stayed air (George Thomas, w146985469; reconcile --fix repaired 0 of 1). The plain roof_flat path writes <material>_slab and is not the bug. Nothing in the dry run checks that a planned block id exists. Not verified: that w146985469 takes the zoned path. Deliver: (1) the zoned flat branch uses block_family_variants(rm)['full']; roof_flat stays on _slab; (2) the dry run prints 'unknown block id <id> x<count>' for every planned id not in the valid block list, naming the source of that list (the minecraft_world block registry or a vendored list); (3) tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py: a zoned flat deepslate_tile roof plans deepslate_tiles, and a made-up id is reported. Check: python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_feature_build passes; a dry run on a spec with a bad id prints the unknown line; after re-applying w146985469 with the spec set back to deepslate_tile, reconcile shows no roof mismatch. Fixes I-027; log the fix on it with check lines for S-035 and S-039.

tasks.title: A zoned feature whose lidar mask comes out empty refuses with a clear message instead of an AttributeError
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the small-building roof-zone crash issue (I-028, snags S-036, S-040); independent review applied. Cause class: Translation. prepare_zones (lib/builds/feature_build.py about lines 1593-1594) sets f.b only 'if roof:'; clear() (about 1603) falls back to f.b whenever zone_roof is falsy. If the readable lidar mask is empty (small building, nDSM mass filter, or the #153 island drop with its 3-cell minimum), f.b is unset and the dry run raises AttributeError. One zone level is not shown to be the trigger (assign_roof_zones accepts one level). Not verified: that the Cycle store (w171869344, 63 columns, one storey) hits this; not reproduced. Deliver: (1) a unit test in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py with a zoned feature, one level and a tiny or low injected zone_data, that reproduces the AttributeError; (2) in prepare_zones, refuse with a plain message naming the feature label, 'no zone cells survived', the 3-cell minimum and the mass threshold, or fall back to the unzoned floor path and print a note; (3) a test for the chosen behaviour, plus a passing one-level zone with enough mass. Check: python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_feature_build passes; the Cycle store dry run with one zone level plans or prints the message, with no traceback. Fixes I-028; log the fix on it with check lines for S-036 and S-040.

tasks.title: An unzoned feature takes its floor from lidar bare terrain, not the live world
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the floor-from-live-world issue (I-029, snags S-037, S-041); independent review applied. Cause class: Translation. floor_y (lib/builds/feature_build.py about lines 1459-1486) takes the median live surface from a ring round the plot and applies max(y, floor_min); build() (about 2479-2482) calls it only for features without zones. Zoned features set f.b from lidar ground (about line 1594). So the live ghost rim sets floor, wall and roof levels on unzoned buildings. Evidence from the snags, not re-verified: Cycle store (w171869344) floor from live surface y52, lidar ground 54, roof 3 blocks below lidar; the designer worked round it with floor_min 55; a door on the east face was pushed into the roof. Source of truth: lidar bare terrain (DTM, as #172), then the designer's floor_min as an override, then the live surface only for transitions (doorstep). Deliver: (1) an unzoned feature's f.b comes from lidar bare-terrain ground under the footprint; floor_min still wins; (1a) state whether a mixed group (mode 'group', takes min f.b over its features, about 2486-2491) keeps that rule; (2) check how _outside_door_floor (about 1927) and its _column_floor fallback behave once unzoned f.b is lidar: keep the live read of the outside surface for the stoop transition only; (3) tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py, including a fixture lidar grid (ground 54, live rim 52) that plans floor 54 with floor_min 55 still winning, and one where the live rim is higher than lidar and the door does not end up inside the roof (many existing fixtures pass floor_min 40-50 and will shift); (4) rules/feature-builds.md updated (floor_min doc about line 48; a floor-source line near 128). Check: python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only test_feature_build passes; the Cycle store dry run without floor_min prints b 54 (needs the lidar cache). Fixes I-029; log the fix with check lines for S-037 and S-041.

tasks.title: Windows are built from facade_plan glazing rows; the legacy facades table is removed
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the windows-ignore-facade-plan issue (I-030, snags S-038, S-042); independent review applied. Cause class: Capability. Build.windows (lib/builds/feature_build.py about line 2237) reads only spec['facades']. facade_plan glazing rows pass validate_glazing_rows (lib/builds/facade_plan.py) but nothing reads them; its docstring (about line 46) says glazing is read 'in a later cleanup'. #130 only added the dry-run report and #131 the pane framing check; neither changed the source of the rows. tasks.title: Roof vents are built as a small capped box, not a lone iron-bars pole

tasks.title: Skylights are recessed into the roof, and only where there is roof, instead of sitting on top
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the skylights-are-glass-boxes issue (I-033, snags S-046, S-054); independent review applied; owner added the edge check. Cause class: Capability (no recessed form). In lib/builds/feature_build.py the skylight kind fills its box with plain glass from the detail's 'at' y, which designers set to the first block above the roof, and _solidify_roof_under makes the roof below a full block, so the glass is a box on the roof, never an opening in it. Not verified: whether designers set 'at' one level too high or the recipe cannot express a recess either way; S-054 is an agent note and decides nothing. Waits for the vents task (#193): both edit _place_detail. Deliver: (1) a skylight replaces the roof's top-level block with glass (a recess); supported cells are not raised above the roof; (2) a skylight must lie fully within the roof: every cell of its box intersects roof at the top level; if any cell is over air or off the roof edge the skylight is not built (no partial skylight) and the dry run prints one line naming the label, position and cells off the roof so the designer moves or shrinks it (builds on #171's solid-roof check, which clips unsupported cells but was written for boxes above the roof); (3) 'at' means roof top level; update the skylight line in rules/building-review.md and rules/feature-builds.md and the redo skill; (4) tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py. Check: a unit test puts skylight glass at roof-top y with nothing above it, and a skylight half over a diagonal roof edge is not built and is reported, and one fully on the roof is recessed; after rebuilding r3176751 and SUSU a block scan finds no glass above the roof surface and none with air beneath. Fixes I-033; log the fix with check lines for S-046 and S-054.

tasks.title: Industrial chimneys are built as hollow round stacks on big roofs, sized from photos and spec, with lidar as a rough check
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from the thin-chimneys issue (I-034, snag S-048, building w66696201); independent review applied. Cause class: Capability. ROOF_DETAIL_KINDS (lib/builds/feature_build.py about line 159) has no chimney kind, so a chimney is a 1x1 'vent'. In w66696201's spec the stacks are 4 'vent' rows (1x2x1 at y77, x6385-6397, z-5556..-5550), described as white cylindrical fume-extract stacks, lidar spike 68-70 m on a 65 m deck (about 3-5 m tall); the notes say the aerial leans about (-1,-6) against lidar. tasks.title: Decor places free-standing hedges the aerial shows (I-035)
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-29 from world issue I-035 (southampton-build): decor hedges come only from the vector map, garden plots and building-border strips, so free-standing aerial hedges never enter the plan. tasks.title: Aerial free-standing hedge detector is off by default (#198 follow-up)
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-29 from a dry run of decor_layer on southampton-build 48,-45. aerial_free_hedges proposed 19 columns, all on carriageway or against buildings (coach and tree shadow), none placeable, and missed the real hedges, which OSM already maps (159 columns) and which are one column wide and flat in lidar. build_decor_plan gains free_hedges=False; the detector runs only when asked. tasks.title: Decor barriers are refused only on carriageway, not on paving, brick or near them
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-29 from a dry run of decor_layer on southampton-build 48,-45: 156 of 159 mapped hedge columns were refused as 'on carriageway', but only 8 neighbouring columns were tarmac; 71 hedge columns stand on live brick/paving and 78 on grass within 2 blocks of paving or brick. Owner decision: the rule should be carriageway only. decor_layer.on_carriageway refuses a barrier column only when its own live ground is tarmac, marking or kerb; the 5x5 near-paving margin and the paving/brick kinds go. Applies to every barrier source. Reason string stays 'on carriageway'. Replaces the #144 brick-path refusal for hedges. Tests in lib/layers/test_decor_layer.py.

tasks.title: Decor uses lidar as a placement and size hint, never as the trigger
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-29 from owner direction after the 48,-45 dry run (201 of 209 unresolved decor items were lone lidar lumps). Rule: a photo, POI, OSM or designer row says there is a feature (statue, wall, hedge, bench, table, anything); decor then consults lidar for placement and size hints. A lump seen only in lidar is ignored: no plan item, not even an unresolved one. decor_plan.lidar_objects stops emitting unlabelled components; a lidar component no longer vetoes OSM/designer furniture unless a photo/aerial label on it names an incompatible kind (e.g. vehicle). Barrier items (map, garden, designer, border) take height from lidar when most columns stand 1-3 above terrain (tree/roof columns excluded); furniture rows carry lidar_height and lidar_cells as hints. Tests in lib/layers/test_decor_plan.py.

tasks.title: feature_build --apply refuses a plan that already has a landed build unless told to overwrite
tasks.notes: Raised 2026-10-28 from an owner observation on west_w34391673. Cause class: Capability. site_kit.apply excludes the plan's own name from the clash check and writes only the new plan's cells, so a re-apply over a landed build leaves old blocks outside the new plan (old roof, stairs, edits). Redo skill now undoes first (e07e331); this is the tool-side guard. feature_build.run: when do_apply and the journal has a landed, not-undone feature entry for spec name, SystemExit pointing at element_undo.py; add --overwrite to opt out. Tests in lib/builds/test_feature_build.py.

tasks.title: redo_here.py runs against any world: world bound before imports, and portal providers load against the current tool
tasks.notes:
Raised 2026-10-29 during `redo decor` in southampton-build. Cause class: Defect. (1) scripts/redo_here.py imports cell_features at module level (line 20), which imports shims/portals.py, which loads the world provider before activate_world_from_args runs, so `redo_here.py --world <name> ...` always dies with 'no world selected'. Fix: bind the world before those imports (or import lazily inside main), same for any other script that imports portals-dependent lib modules at top level (grep for scripts calling add_world_arg after such imports). (2) With the world bound, worlds/southampton-build/providers/uos-portals/portals.py line 34 does `from osgb import in_bounds, load_offsets, to_mc` and lib/geo/osgb.py has no in_bounds: provider and tool have drifted. tasks.title: cell_registry reconcile blows up to ~7.5 GB: bound the LiveBlocks cache and add a region-file read path
tasks.notes:
Raised 2026-10-29. `python3 scripts/cell_registry.py --world southampton-build reconcile` (dry run) ran 25+ min with a 7.5 GB physical footprint (vmmap; ps RSS showed only ~700 MB because the rest was compressed) and had to be killed. Cause class: Defect (suspected from reading the code; NOT yet measured, so confirm with tracemalloc or a capped run first). Dry run goes run_reconcile -> open_registry(blocks=site_kit.live_blocks()) -> LiveBlocks (lib/blocks/block_store.py), which reads over MCP block_scan_region. LiveBlocks._scan_box writes a self._cache entry for EVERY position in each scanned tile (air and unrequested blocks included, tuple key + str), and _cache is only cleared on flush(), so one reconcile over every journalled cell accumulates the whole scanned volume. (A) CACHE: cache only the positions callers asked for (or store tiles compactly, e.g. per-section arrays / palette indices), and evict between cells: CellRegistry.reconcile reads each cell independently via _classify/_bad, so a per-cell clear (or an LRU cap) is safe; keep the flush()/mark_written stale-read guard intact. Check other long loops that call read_many across many cells (ensure, _upgrade_mismatched, _ghost_needs) for the same growth. (B) REGION FILES: lib/blocks/region_blocks.py already has a read-only RegionBlocks(BlockStore) over .mca files, authorised for planning and dry-run reads after server save (see its docstring: ADR 004 exception, 2026-10-26). Make the reconcile DRY RUN read through RegionBlocks (after one server_save_all_worlds via the existing flusher/settle) instead of MCP, since it is far faster; keep `--fix` and all post-write readback on LiveBlocks/MCP (RegionBlocks is never a restore or write path and must stay strictly read-only). Likely shape: a site_kit helper (e.g. disk_blocks() beside live_blocks()) that saves, then returns RegionBlocks.from_world_config(); run_reconcile uses it when not fix. Check RegionBlocks itself is not unbounded: it holds _files (whole .mca bytes) and _chunks dicts until flush(), so cap or clear those per cell too. Mind semantic differences: RegionBlocks returns None for a missing chunk and minecraft:air for a missing section, which _classify maps to 'missing' vs air; confirm drift output is identical between the two stores on a small cell set. DELIVERABLE: dry-run reconcile on southampton-build finishes in minutes with peak footprint well under 1 GB (state the before/after numbers), and drift findings match the MCP path on a sample of cells; tests in lib/blocks/test_block_store.py (cache bounded across many tiles; no entries for unrequested positions) and scripts/test_cell_registry.py or lib/journal/test_cell_journal.py (dry run uses the disk store, --fix still uses MCP); ship via a task/* branch and ship_branch.py merge.
2026-10-29 completed: merged locally via ship_branch.py as2a0ac8a (9d7fba2, f4e7a36), independent review APPROVE. Reproduction:32 requested positions over16 sparse tiles retained1,048,576 entries and112.18MiB traced memory before; after32 entries and0.231MiB peak. LiveBlocks bulk scans retain requested positions only; cache capped at65,536 blocks including scalar section prefetch, preserving mark_written/flush refusal. Dry-run reconcile saves/settles once through the live identity/flusher path then uses read-only RegionBlocks; fix/readback remain live. Region file/chunk LRUs capped at2/256. Full-world run exposed additional journal retention (4.3GB physical peak even after block-store fix); decoded plan cache now capped at262,144 positions and16 plans, ownership cache retains one cell. This also bounds the shared caches used by ensure and mismatched upgrades; ghost-needs itself does not read blocks. Final Southampton dry run across61 journal cells:189.35s real,723,550,208 bytes max RSS,756,483,104 bytes peak physical footprint (~721MiB), versus ticket baseline25+min/~7.5GB. Existing drift:84 missing blocks in7 cells,93 foreign in4 cells;11 findings, no block writes. Three complete sample cells52,-42 /52,-41 /52,-44 had identical clean disk/MCP Drift results (disk6.54s, MCP209.77s including shared-rate-limit waits). tasks.title: Closed issues and their snag pictures are archived into registry/issues-closed.json, automatically at the end of a sherlock run
tasks.notes:
Raised 2026-10-28 from an owner question (does sherlock move closed issues to a side file? No). Independent review applied. Cause class: Capability. issues.py has no archive step: confirmed and wontfix issues stay in <world>/registry/issues.json for good. Measured on southampton-build: issues.json 184 KB, registry/issues/img/ 92 MB (the pictures are the bulk). Prior art: #120 (issues lib and CLI), #152 (hold/unfix, same module). Not the same thing as lib/site/site_archive.py and scripts/site_archive.py, which archive site/ISSUES.txt into site/archive/ISSUES-closed.txt; say so in the new command's help text and docstring. Only issue_log.py and issues.py read issues.json in code; registry_next.py, cell_journal.py and cell_registry.py mention it in comments only; site_pages.py does not read it. DELIVERABLE (a) command and library: 1. `issues.py archive` moves every issue at confirmed or wontfix from issues.json to registry/issues-closed.json, unchanged (ID, snags, fix log, verdicts); fix-landed and open never move. 2. Pictures of moved snags move from issues/img/ to issues/img-closed/ and each snag's image path is rewritten; verify resolves live paths under img and closed paths under img-closed. 3. list, digest and sync read the live file only (digest counts are unaffected by design). show and match also search the closed file; optional list --all. 4. Every mutating command (add snag, verdict, unfix, hold, diagnose, move, merge) finds the issue in either file; anything that sets an archived issue back to open or fix-landed moves it and its pictures back to the live file in the same write. merge and move across files fold the closed issue into the live one (state the rule in the code). 5. Counters next_issue and next_snag stay in the live file only, are never reset, and archive leaves them alone; the closed file carries none. IDs are never reused. 6. Safety: re-read both files right before writing; move picture files first, write the closed file, then the live file, so a crash leaves a duplicate that verify catches, never a loss. verify checks: no ID in both files, no dangling image path in either. 7. Update comment-only mentions in registry_next.py, cell_journal.py, cell_registry.py (no logic change). DELIVERABLE (b) skill and docs text: 8. Sherlock Close the case gets a new step 2, `issues.py archive`, run automatically after verify says OK, then verify again; either failing: report and stop; one report line 'archived N closed issues'; later steps renumber 3-7. The world commit adds only paths that exist among registry/issues.json registry/issues-closed.json registry/issues/img registry/issues/img-closed. Update the sherlock skill's reading line and path list, snag/SKILL.md line 6, rules/process.md line 19, templates/new-world-site/{NOTES,README,ISSUES}.txt and the issues.py docstring. FILES: scripts/issues.py, lib/journal/issue_log.py, lib/journal/test_issue_log.py, .claude/skills/sherlock/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/snag/SKILL.md, rules/process.md, templates/new-world-site/NOTES.txt, README.txt, ISSUES.txt, comment-only in the three registry modules. CHECKS: (a) `python3 scripts/run_tests.py --only issue_log` passes with new tests: archive moves confirmed and wontfix only; add snag on a closed issue reopens it and returns its pictures; merge across files; match finds a closed issue; archive everything then add a new issue and a new snag gives higher IDs than before; verify catches an ID in both files and a dangling picture; digest counts are the same before and after. Run these on a temporary world copy, not live Southampton. (b) The owner runs a sherlock close on Southampton once after merge: before and after counts of confirmed plus wontfix issues, `du` of registry/issues/img, `issues.py verify` OK, `show` of an archived issue still prints with its pictures, the commit holds only the world's issue-record paths. Risk: the world checkout is shared with other sessions, hence the re-read before writing.

tasks.title: Allow evidence-backed tree rooting on hard surfaces and one-block edge shunts
tasks.notes:
Accepted tree shunt plan: replace lawn-only/material allowlists with evidence-led rooting, following the revised decor approach. Concrete or other hard surface alone must not reject an evidenced tree; allow lawns, gravel, paved courtyards, plazas and pavements, including unresolved small planting pits. Trunks must not root in carriageway or water; apply that check to the trunk ground footprint, not the crown centre or canopy footprint. When an evidenced trunk falls on the edge of carriageway/water, allow at most one block of adjustment onto an immediately adjacent valid rooting position. Choose deterministically, keep the canopy aligned with the observed crown as closely as possible, and record the original position, adjusted position and reason. Never chain adjustments or move farther until a tree fits. If no valid position exists within one block, leave unplaced with a review reason. Canopies may overhang carriageway, water and neighbouring cells subject to existing collision, ownership and mask rules; #218 already permits leaf-only overhang into unprepared neighbours. Preserve feature-zone protection and trunk ownership within the planting cell; do not change ground merely to legalize a tree. Align foliage rules, planners/review images and reports; add synthetic tests for legal hard ground, successful one-block edge shunt, no legal neighbour, maximum distance, deterministic choice, blocked trunk and unaffected canopy overhang. Backlog only; not implemented.
Refinement 2026-10-31: target lib/layers/trees_layer.py plan_cell and the existing tree review/replan paths. Current code already grants some paved surfaces and feature-zone exceptions to aerial/mapped crowns; preserve those evidenced exceptions rather than accidentally tightening them. Identify which crown sources count as evidenced and keep detector/dense-fill policy unchanged. Evaluate carriageway/water using the existing semantic map and live surface checks; hard-surface material alone is neither evidence of a road nor proof of legal rooting. Missing surface/unknown water status must produce a review reason, not a guessed height.
For the edge adjustment, use a horizontal displacement of at most one block from the accepted pre-shunt trunk position: same position first, then the four orthogonally adjacent positions (no diagonals or chained search). Apply all trunk, cell-boundary, feature-zone/explicit exception, collision and mask checks to each candidate; never shift just to dodge a blocked trunk on otherwise legal ground. Choose the smallest displacement from the observed crown, with a documented stable coordinate tie-break. Keep this shunt separate from existing lidar/crown snapping and report both so successive stages cannot conceal movement. Extend existing plan/review artifacts with original/final trunk and reason; retain current readers. Synthetic acceptance includes cell-edge refusal and existing courtyard exceptions as well as the listed hard-ground/shunt/overhang cases.
Completed 2026-11-01: explicit aerial/mapped/extra crowns use evidence-led hard-ground rooting, with common trunk-footprint road/water guards and at-most-one orthogonal edge shunt. Every candidate preserves cell/ownership/mask/collision gates; missing/unknown ground is a review reason. Stable observed-crown distance/coordinate tie-break; aligned per-retained-crown observations survive snapping and mapped precedence. Reports/review image/replan JSON retain existing readers and expose both snap and root stages. Detector material/generation rules remain restrictive and never shunt; leaf overhang unchanged. Resolve relative CLI spec paths against the explicit world's root and preserve absolute paths; document this rule and remove cwd dependence. Before any undo, validate the builder/spec exists and the current spec validates; a missing or invalid builder stops without clearing the feature. For valid reapply, follow undo-first and lock/readback/recovery requirements; do not silently pass --overwrite or edit/migrate an invalid spec. tasks.notes:

Cause: ground.classify uses map/aerial colours and generic shade filling without garden plot or entrance intent; guessed lawn near any road/building can become paving. garden_sources already grows approximate plots and consumes street/per-property boundary conventions, but Kitchener's convention has selected hedge vetoes and no front fence/wall specification. Boundary generation reserves no entrance gaps or connections. The saved decor report consists of aerial hedges and mapped iron bars. Deliver one shared residential frontage description consumed by the existing ground and decor passes: private frontage extent/surface, boundary segments, entrance opening and connection. Reuse existing plots/segments and convention files; no new pass or parallel geometry engine. Use lib/site/provenance.py and existing evidence IDs, retaining property/street scope and reason for inference through plans/reports. Replace the lossy garden tuple/provenance conversion and superseded access-blind joining path.
Evidence: explicit property observation > street-run evidence > labelled deterministic same-street inference. Owner prefers a coherent realistic street from best available evidence over leaving gaps because exact detail is uncertain. Inferred private frontages require identified residential properties and supporting frontage/street evidence; missing conventions alone do not authorize fences. Explicit open frontages, none vetoes and per-house overrides win. Do not randomize surfaces for variety. Retain observed gravel/paving/green differences and distinguish private frontage from public pavement; constrain generic guessed-lawn conversion accordingly. Nonresidential/campus behaviour must remain compatible.
Pass responsibility: feature owns the building/porch, threshold and feature-generated external landing/steps/supports, even outside the mapped footprint. Keep existing placement and journal ownership semantics. Expose a small shared read-only entrance-approach description: actual door, feature approach extent, usable outward connection point/height/direction, clearance and provenance; distinguish generated door positions from observed ones. Ground owns remaining frontage/pavement surfaces and onward route, joining the outer end of the feature approach (door when no approach), without duplicating or replacing feature steps. Decor owns boundary/furniture/gate placement and preserves the route/opening/headroom; it does not construct a second threshold, stair or path. Respect existing trees.
Solid feature steps/landings/supports retain journal ownership. Required clear space is shared semantic planning data, not ownership of air: preserve journal CANCEL/air-cancels rules. Ground/decor must not fill reserved clearance or replace feature solids. Reserve access across mapped, convention, designer and aerial candidates AND final join_pieces/straightening. Explain conflicts with explicit observed boundaries rather than silently erasing them. Preserve lidar heights, masks, ownership, clipping and undo. Blocked connections report endpoints, responsible pass and reason; do not bypass protected blocks or alter the house to force access.
Legacy approaches: use narrowly scoped read-only reconstruction from the landed plan/journal where trustworthy; otherwise label generated/inferred data and unavailable endpoints. A plausible inferred entrance may guide the frontage but cannot be reported as a verified connection to an actual door. Refresh the approach description from current geometry after feature rebuilds; avoid stale copied endpoints. No broad feature/staircase redesign, ownership migration or generic reapply/provenance/cross-cell policy change.
Scope: lib/sources/garden_sources.py, lib/layers/ground_layer.py, decor_plan.py, decor_layer.py and their existing tests; narrowly scoped approach description in lib/builds/house_build.py and feature_build.py plus existing plan/journal metadata only as needed; rules/frontage-and-evidence.md and rules/handoff-layered-passes.md. tasks.title: site_lock.run crashes on macOS with PermissionError in its process-group cleanup and leaves the lock held (redo_layer.py)
tasks.notes:
Seen 2026-11-09 on every `scripts/redo_layer.py --apply` run after the layers had applied and verified (southampton-build, macOS): traceback ends at lib/site/site_lock.py run(), `os.killpg(process.pid, 0)` in the post-exit grace loop, `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted`. Only ProcessLookupError is caught, so on macOS (killpg on a group whose leader has exited can give EPERM, not ESRCH) the finally block aborts before the SIGKILL and `release(owner)`. Effects: the lock stays held by the redo-layer-<pid> owner (a later redo on another cell refuses with 'Held by redo-layer-N'), and the command exits 1 although the work succeeded. Workaround: `site_lock.py --world W release redo-layer-<pid>`. Also note `site_lock.py run ... -- redo_layer.py` cannot wrap redo_layer because it claims the lock itself ('Held by claude'). Fix: treat PermissionError like ProcessLookupError in both killpg calls, always reach release(owner) (nest in try/finally), and add a unit test with a mocked killpg raising PermissionError. Consider making redo_layer honour an existing SITE_OWNER instead of claiming a second lock.

Closed at 0ee7f37627d26068018eda1fca6fc3589bf8f0cb: Cleanup handles PermissionError at all killpg sites and nests release in finally; cleanup errors cannot bypass lock release. redo_layer validates and honours inherited SITE_OWNER instead of claiming a second lock. tasks.title: Trees and decor stand on lidar terrain height, not the live surface (a roof) (I-046, I-038)
tasks.notes:
Serves "Trees stand on a roof" (I-046; two snags: two trees on West's roof and two on a flat roof near Retail, cell 48,-44) and the decor-on-an-overhanging-roof issue (I-038; S-064, S-066). Owner direction (2026-11-16): the cure for a roof overhang is to build trees and decor on the true ground level, not to remove them and not to skip the column; building them from game-world heights rather than lidar heights "is asking for trouble". Trees may use the air around a feature (leaves can hang in air beside or above a roof or wall) but may not replace any block a feature owns. Precedent: #167 (ground from lidar terrain), #172, #204 (door floors from lidar ground), #206 (the veto this task replaces).

Cause (code read; the measurement was not replayed in a test).
- Trees: lib/layers/trees_layer.py `candidate()` takes the trunk base from `surface_y(world, x, z)`, the live top non-plant block, so a roof counts as ground. The 'feature zone' rule (`fp` / `ground_cols`) is skipped for evidenced crowns (aerial, surveyed, extra: `observed`), so an evidenced crown over a roof is planted on it. Measured 2026-11-16: a trees+decor redo of 48,-44 (readback 0 mismatches) left exactly the same 215 oak_leaves and 5 oak_log beside West's roof, so a fresh pass places them there again. Not verified: how each of those crowns was sourced. The trees layer has no lidar terrain grid today; its lidar use is the canopy (nDSM) snapping only.
- Decor: lib/layers/decor_layer.py also stands on `surface_y`; since #206 it refuses a column whose live surface is more than 2 blocks above terrain (`above_lidar_ground`, reason 'above lidar ground'). That removes the item; it does not move it to the ground.

Change.
1. One shared helper (for example `ground_at(world, lidar_hm, x, z)` in surface_probe) returns the terrain block Y for a column and the block at that Y. Trunk base, decor base and every material, water, carriageway and 'uneven trunk ground' check read the block at terrain Y through it, never `surface_y` (over a roof `surface_y`, `column_ground_kind` and the carriageway test all return the roof block). Both layers use it.
2. The block at terrain Y must be solid, unowned ground; otherwise the item is unplaced with the reason 'no ground at terrain' (no floating trunk or decor). Warm the prefetch for the terrain-Y reads (#110/#263 stalls).

tasks.notes:
Found in #244 (2026-11-16). `python3 scripts/decor_layer.py --world W --cell C` (dry run) on a cell that is already built treats the cell's own decor mask as blocked, so it understates the plan: #244 reported 305 blocks on 53,-43 instead of about 2,716 and every front hedge failed as 'blocked by live or owned block' (numbers from #244, not re-measured; the last real apply, world commit 8447beb on 2026-11-14, placed 2,695). Causes (read from the code on main, 2026-11-19):
- Understating: the own mask's positions are in the `masked` set AND the live world still holds the old blocks, so both the mask test and the `is_air` test refuse the cell's own columns. Subtracting the mask alone is not enough.
- Overwriting: `write_report(name, ...)` writes `verification/site/<name>-report.json` in the dry run and again in `apply_cell`, so a dry run replaces the last apply's report. The preview, crowns, plan and kinds files are written only by dry runs, into the same tracked folder.
- Trees crash: `Plan.bounds()` does `zip(*self.cells)` and raises on an empty plan; `trees_layer.run` calls `preview` and `apply(dry=True)` unconditionally, where decor guards with `if placed:`.
- Note: layer_redo.py is NOT the precedent: it shells out to `mask_undo.py --apply` (a real undo). The precedent is scripts/trees_replan.py `replan()`: `plan_undo` for the cleared positions, `PlannedWorld(Plan, world, ignore=cleared)` so old blocks read as air, and `TreeInputs.after_undo(remaining_masks)`.

Change:
1. Decor dry run plans as if the cell's own decor mask were undone, as trees_replan does for trees. Factor the shared part of `trees_replan.replan` (own-mask cleared positions via `pass_mask.plan_undo`, a `PlannedWorld` whose ignore set is those positions, masked set = every other mask) into one helper that trees_replan and the decor dry run both use; do not write a second copy. If `plan_undo` reports conflicts, the dry run says so and plans against the unmodified world (it must not raise). Real apply and redo keep their present behaviour.
2. Trees dry run uses the same helper, so it too plans as if its own trees mask were undone (today it does not, which is why trees_replan.py exists). Ground dry run: no change to planning; it reports mask conflicts on purpose ('NOT SAFE TO APPLY: undo the listed mask first') and hiding them would be wrong. Say in the commit message that ground was checked.
3. A dry run writes only `-dry` names: `<name>-dry-report.json`, `<name>-dry-preview.png` (trees also `<name>-dry-crowns.png`, `<name>-dry-plan.json`; ground `<name>-dry-kinds.png`, `<name>-dry-preview.png`). Add a `dry` flag to `write_report` and build every artifact path through one helper so tests can redirect it (several paths are hard-coded from ROOT today). Apply keeps the present names. A dry run never writes an apply-named file.
4. Empty plan in the trees dry run: do not call `preview` or `apply(dry=True)` when nothing is placed; print that no preview was written (as decor does).
Out of scope: restoring the tracked 53,-43 files the earlier dry runs overwrote (a checkout of world commit 8447beb's versions; the owner's call); the world's .gitignore. Not a stretch by the model-and-effort rules only if the shared helper stays small; if it grows into a rewrite of trees_replan, stop and report.
